titulo: The task battery for your site (map + generator)
lead: Time to put it together: the tasks that matter on your site, each with a contract, steps, and what to expect, in a battery that the dry-run robot runs on every change and that your agent can run whenever you want. conferir-bateria.mjs tells you if it is ready; the map and the generator organize what is missing.
objetivo: build the task battery for your site and check that each task has a contract, proof, and stop.

secoes.titulo: From the template to your battery

texto: The ones that make money or cause headaches: finding a price, seeing available times, getting to the contact page. Start read-only.
Each task is a contract: a goal tied to the page, limits with a "no", proof in quotes, a stop with a number.
The robot understands four steps: abrir, preencher [label, value], escolher [label, option], and clicar [button or link text]. All by name from the tree.
If a step can't find the control by name, the problem is usually the HTML (course 0, lesson 3), not the battery.
At least one task with "espera": "parar": your site's login, verification, or confirmation. It proves the test stops where it should.
The checker rejects a battery with no stop.
On your local site (at 127.0.0.1, on your project's port) or a staging site. The checker warns you when the address is not local.
No production with real data, purchases, or submissions.

exemplo.texto: A frozen battery and regression testing for when WebMCP changes again are covered in course 5. Your battery is the starting point.

degraus.titulo: Lesson 6 · An agent tests the site

txt.titulo: Plan — Browser agents: test the site the way the agent sees it
txt.travou: ## What got stuck and what I decided

perguntas.p: The checker rejected your battery with "nenhuma tarefa com espera parar". Why does it require that?
opcoes: Because the dry-run robot only runs with a stop
Because a reading task always ends in a stop
To prove the test stops where it should
Because Playwright MCP needs a stop
perguntas.explica: A battery with no stop never tests whether the agent respects login, verification, and confirmation, which are the points where a mistake costs the most.

perguntas.p: A step preencher ["E-mail", …] failed because the robot couldn't find the field by its label. Where is the most likely problem?
opcoes: In the HTML: the field has no label that becomes a name
In the dry-run robot, which doesn't read email fields
In the kit's Chromium, which is too old
In the battery, which should use the field's id
perguntas.explica: The robot finds it by the accessibility tree name, just like the agent. A field with no label has no reliable name: the fix is in the HTML (course 0, lesson 3).

opcoes: In production, because that's where the customer browses
On any site similar to yours
On a competitor's site, to compare
On your local or staging site
perguntas.explica: A test agent only runs against your own site, local or staging. Production has real data; a third party's site isn't yours to automate.

itens.texto: 3 to 6 tasks, each with a contract, steps, and what you expect.
Proves the test stops at login, verification, or confirmation.
The dry-run robot after every change; your agent whenever you want, checked by format.
